desc:
Children stand in a line and child i has rating ratings[i]. Every child gets at least one candy. For two adjacent children:

  • if one has a strictly higher rating, that child must receive strictly more candies;
  • if the ratings are equal, both must receive exactly the same number of candies.

Return the minimum total number of candies.

ratings = [1,2,2]    -> 5
ratings = [1,3,3,2]  -> 6
ratings = [4,4,4]    -> 3

In the first example the two children rated 2 must get the same amount, and they are above the child rated 1, so the candies are 1, 2, 2.
hints: Children with equal ratings next to each other must behave identically. Treat a maximal run of equal ratings as a single unit.
After merging runs, neighbouring units always have different ratings, so you are back to a classic two-direction candy problem on the units.

Compute the minimum candy per unit with a left-to-right and a right-to-left pass (take the maximum of both), then multiply each unit's candy by the number of children in the run and add everything up.
editorial: Compress consecutive equal ratings into runs, keeping the length of each run. All children of a run get the same number of candies, and the only constraints that remain are between neighbouring runs, whose ratings differ.

On the runs, do the usual two sweeps: left to right give c[i] = c[i-1] + 1 when the run rating exceeds the previous one (else 1), then right to left raise c[i] to c[i+1] + 1 when the run rating exceeds the next one and it is not already larger. Each run's value is the smallest allowed, so the total sum(c[i] * length[i]) is minimal. O(n) time and space.
